The '''1930 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 44th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]'s premier inter-county hurling tournament. The championship began on 18 May 1930 and ended on 7 September 1930.

[[Cork GAA|Cork]] entered the championship as the [[1929 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]], however, they were defeated by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the Munster semi-final.

On 7 September 1930, [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] won the championship following a 5–06 to 3–06 victory over [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] in the [[1930 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]] at [[Croke Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |title=All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Roll of Honour |publisher=The GAA website |access-date=25 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110905085701/http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |archive-date=5 September 2011 }}</ref> This was their 11th championship title overall and their first title since [[1925 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1925]].

==Teams==

A total of twelve teams contested the championship, the same number of participants from the [[1929 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|previous championship]]. There were no new entrants.

==Championship statistics==
===Miscellaneous===

* On 13 July 1930, the Munster semi-final between [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] and [[Waterford]] ended in disarray after the referee, [[Seán Óg Murphy]], attempted to send off [[John Ware (hurler)|John]] and [[Charlie Ware Snr|Charlie Ware]] of Waterford and [[John Joe Callanan]] of Tipperary. The Waterford players refused to leave and there was a delay of 12 minutes. The referee awarded the match to Tipperary.
* Tipperary become the first team to win the Triple Crown of hurling by winning the All-Ireland titles in the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|senior]], [[All-Ireland Junior Hurling Championship|junior]] and [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor]] grades.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.premierview.ie/famous_feats.html |title=Famous feats |publisher=Premier View website |access-date=11 December 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120824141557/http://www.premierview.ie/famous_feats.html |archive-date=24 August 2012 }}</ref>
